Classic Hanukkah Braised Brisket

Served at: Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 3 hours 30 min

Braised brisket is a beloved centerpiece for many Hanukkah celebrations, symbolizing warmth, family, and abundance during the Festival of Lights. Its slow-cooked tenderness and rich, savory gravy make it a comforting and deeply flavorful dish, perfect for gathering loved ones around the holiday table.

Ingredients

  • 1 (4-5 pound / 1.8-2.3 kg) beef brisket, flat cut, trimmed of excess hard fat
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil or vegetable oil
  • 2 large yellow onions, thinly sliced
  • 4 carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) chunks
  • 3 celery stalks, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) chunks
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) tomato paste
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dry red wine (such as Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon)
  • 3 cups (720 ml) beef broth or stock
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, freshly ground, plus more to taste
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
  2. Pat the brisket dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season generously all over with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.
  3. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear the brisket fat-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply browned and a crust forms. Flip and sear the other side for another 5-7 minutes. Remove brisket from the pot and set aside.
  4. Add the sliced onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and tomato paste, and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring constantly until fragrant.
  5. Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Let it simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
  6. Return the brisket to the pot, placing it fat-side up on top of the vegetables. Pour in the beef broth and water. Add the bay leaves and dried thyme.
  7. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer on the stovetop. Cover the Dutch oven tightly with its lid.
  8. Transfer the Dutch oven to the preheated oven and braise for 3 to 3.5 hours, or until the brisket is fork-tender. The exact time will depend on the thickness of your brisket.
  9. Remove the Dutch oven from the oven. Carefully transfer the brisket to a cutting board, tent with foil, and let it rest for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing. This resting period is crucial for juicy meat.
  10. While the brisket rests, skim any excess fat from the surface of the braising liquid. You can serve the vegetables and sauce as is, or for a smoother sauce, strain the liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on the solids to extract all the flavor. Discard the solids, then return the sauce to the pot and simmer briefly to reduce if desired. Taste and adjust seasoning.
  11. Slice the brisket against the grain into 1/4-inch (0.6 cm) thick slices. Arrange on a platter, spoon the sauce and vegetables over the top, and garnish with fresh parsley if using. Serve hot.

Tips

  • Make Ahead: Brisket is even better the next day! Prepare it a day in advance, let it cool completely, then refrigerate. The next day, remove the solidified fat from the top, slice the cold brisket, and reheat gently in the sauce.
  • Slicing Technique: Always slice brisket against the grain. This shortens the muscle fibers, making the meat much more tender and easier to chew.
  • Flavor Boost: For a touch of sweetness, add 1/4 cup (60 ml) of dried prunes or dried apricots along with the liquids before braising.
